newsitem.title: CHINA: Yuan ends up at 26-month high vs U.S. dollar.
newsitem.headline: Yuan ends up at 26-month high vs U.S. dollar.

text.p: The Chinese yuan closed up on Tuesday at a 26-month high of 8.2895 against the dollar, with a large sale of dollars from a single major bank breaching the cap of 8.2900 set by the central bank, dealers said.
The central bank did not intervene to depress the local currency, resulting in the smooth breaching of the cap, dealers said.
"The offer of the dollars from one major bank pushed the yuan up," one dealer said. "The bank was seen in urgent need of local currency."

"Most banks were holding excess dollars following the settlement of foreign currency, but the central bank had held down the yuan below the 8.2900 level over the past few weeks," another dealer said, referring to requirements to enterprises to turn over their foreign currency to banks.
"Today's rises were partly attributable to the absence of intervention by the central bank," he said.

The yuan opened higher at 8.2905 and moved around the opening level for most of the session, hitting an intraday low of 8.2907 before rising in late trading. Trading was active with most deals done at about 8.2904, dealers said.
The weighted average price on Monday was 8.2905.
If the yuan could hold firm above the 8.2900 level, further rises were expected in the near term, otherwise the currency would continue to consolidate below that level, dealers said.
The yuan closed lower at 7.0001 from 6.9900 against 100 Japanese yen and ended up at 1.0699 from 1.0702 against the Hong Kong dollar.
